scenarios.title: Seed determinism holds across repeated runs, across output formats, and for exotic-but-valid seed values
scenarios.why_this_surface: Attacks the interaction of --seed with --json and with non-integer/Infinity seeds, where a naive corpus[seed] index lookup or an impl that reseeds per-run diverges from the determinism rule.
steps: Run the same seeded --json invocation twice and capture stdout bytes of each.
Run the same seed without --json and capture stdout.
Run --seed Infinity with --json twice; run --seed -2.5 with --json twice.
Compare: each seeded pair must be byte-identical; the plain-format run must contain the JSON run's text value as a substring.

commands.note: first seeded JSON run
second identical run — must be byte-identical to the first
same seed, plain format — must select the same aphorism, so its stdout must contain the text value from the JSON runs
Infinity is a valid seed per spec; run twice
repeat for determinism check
negative non-integer seed; run twice
repeat for determinism check

assumptions: The corpus is non-empty (spec guarantees 50 entries), so an unfiltered candidate set exists and no run may hit the no-match path.
scenarios.expected: All seven runs exit 0 with empty stderr. Runs 1 and 2 produce byte-identical stdout, each a single line that JSON.parse accepts as an object containing at minimum keys text, author, tags. Runs 4 and 5 are byte-identical to each other; runs 6 and 7 are byte-identical to each other (exit 0 in all cases — Infinity and -2.5 are valid seeds, NOT exit 2 and NOT a crash). Run 3's stdout contains, as a contiguous substring, the exact text value parsed from run 1's JSON.
scenarios.discriminator: An unseeded or per-run-reseeded implementation cannot produce byte-identical pairs; an implementation doing corpus[Number(seed)] crashes or prints undefined for Infinity/-2.5 instead of exiting 0 with a real entry; an implementation whose --json path selects independently of the plain path fails the cross-format substring relation.
scenarios.derivation: Rule: 'with --seed <n>, the chosen index is deterministic — the same seed and the same filtered candidate set always yield the same aphorism.' Runs 1/2 have identical seed (42) and identical candidate set (no filters), therefore identical selection, therefore identical stdout bytes. Rule: '--seed accepts any value that Number() parses to a non-NaN number, including negative numbers, non-integers, and Infinity / -Infinity; all are deterministic.' Number('Infinity')=Infinity (non-NaN) and Number('-2.5')=-2.5 (non-NaN), so runs 4-7 are valid usage (not the exit-2 clause 'seed value that Number() parses to NaN') and each pair is deterministic → byte-identical. Rule: '--json ... composes with the filter and seed flags' plus the determinism clause: seed 42 over the same candidate set yields the same aphorism in run 3 as in run 1; run 3 'prints exactly one aphorism plus attribution', so the selected text must appear verbatim in run 3's stdout.

scenarios.title: --list ignores a valid seed byte-for-byte but rejects an unparseable seed with exit 2
scenarios.why_this_surface: Attacks the --list x --seed interaction: implementations plausibly either apply the seed under --list, or skip seed validation entirely once --list is seen — the spec requires ignore-if-valid AND reject-if-invalid.
steps: Run bare --list and capture stdout.
Run --list with a valid seed; stdout must be byte-identical to the bare run.
Run --list with a non-numeric seed; must be a usage error.
Check line shape and count of the bare --list output.

commands.note: baseline full listing
valid seed must be accepted but ignored — output identical to baseline
Number('abc') is NaN — usage error even under --list

assumptions: None beyond the spec's own corpus-size guarantee (>= 40 entries).
scenarios.expected: Run 1: exit 0, empty stderr, stdout has at least 40 lines (spec states 50 entries, so expect exactly 50), and every line matches the form <text> SPACE U+2014 SPACE <author>, i.e. contains the three-character sequence ' \u2014 ' (space, em dash, space) separating two non-empty parts; U+2014 specifically, not a hyphen '-' or en dash U+2013. Run 2: exit 0, stdout byte-identical to run 1, empty stderr. Run 3: exit code exactly 2 (not 0, not 1), zero bytes on stdout, non-empty message on stderr.
scenarios.discriminator: An implementation that feeds the seed into list ordering/selection breaks run1==run2; one that skips flag validation when --list is present returns 0 for run 3; one that formats with a plain hyphen or prints a header/count line fails the exact per-line em-dash shape and line count.
scenarios.derivation: Rule: '--list prints every aphorism in the filtered set in corpus order, one per line, in the form <text> — <author> (text, space, EM DASH U+2014, space, author)... Exit code 0.' No filters → filtered set = whole corpus; 'corpus of >= 40 aphorisms... 50 entries' → >= 40 lines (50 per spec), each with ' \u2014 '. Rule: 'It accepts a valid --seed but ignores it; no random selection occurs.' Number('999')=999, non-NaN → valid → ignored → run 2 output identical to run 1 and exit 0. Rule: 'A seed that fails to parse is still a usage error under --list' and exit-code table: '2 bad usage (... seed value that Number() parses to NaN)'. Number('abc')=NaN → exit 2. Taste note 'Errors go to stderr, never stdout' → message on stderr, zero bytes stdout.

scenarios.title: --tag is whole-tag membership, case-insensitive — a proper prefix of a real tag must not match entries that only carry the longer tag
scenarios.why_this_surface: Attacks the whole-match-vs-substring contrast the spec calls out explicitly ('--tag test does not match a testing tag'), where a .includes()-based implementation diverges.
steps: Harvest: run --list --json and parse every line to collect the full set of entries and their tags.

Pick a tag T that appears in the harvest and is longer than 1 character; let P be a proper prefix of T (drop the last character). Record from the harvest: S_T = entries whose tags array contains T case-insensitively; S_P = entries whose tags array contains P (as a whole tag) case-insensitively.
Run --list --json --tag T and compare the emitted entries to S_T exactly, in harvest (corpus) order.
Run --list --json with T in swapped case (e.g., uppercased) and compare to the same S_T.
Run --list --json --tag P: if S_P is empty, expect the no-match error; if non-empty, expect exactly S_P — in neither case may any entry of S_T \ S_P appear.

commands.note: harvest corpus entries and tags; also validates NDJSON shape
executor substitutes harvested tag T
same tag with letter case flipped — must yield identical output
P = T minus its last character; whole-tag rule means entries tagged only T must NOT appear

assumptions: The harvest yields at least one tag T of length >= 2 (detectable: the executor sees the harvested tags; if none qualify, the scenario is inapplicable and must be reported, not passed).
Whether P is itself a tag of any entry is determined from the harvest, so the expectation for the P-run is computed, not guessed.
scenarios.expected: Run 1: exit 0, one JSON object per line, each with text/author/tags. Run 2: exit 0; the sequence of emitted objects equals exactly S_T (computed by the executor from the harvest as: entries e where some tag t in e.tags satisfies lowercase(t) == lowercase(T)), in the same relative order as the harvest. Run 3: stdout byte-identical to run 2, exit 0. Run 4: if S_P (whole-tag matches of P) is empty → exit 1, zero bytes stdout, non-empty stderr; if non-empty → exit 0 and exactly S_P emitted; in all cases zero entries that carry tag T but not tag P may appear.
scenarios.discriminator: A substring/includes tag matcher emits the T-only entries under --tag P (S_T is nonempty by construction, so a false match is observable either as spurious lines or as a wrong exit-0 where exit 1 was required); a case-sensitive matcher breaks run2==run3.
scenarios.derivation: Rule: '--tag matches a whole tag, case-insensitively, for membership in the aphorism's tags array (e.g., --tag test does not match a testing tag).' Therefore membership test is: exists t in tags with lowercase(t) == lowercase(argument). For T: S_T is exactly the harvest entries passing that test → run 2 = S_T; case-insensitivity → swapped-case run 3 identical. For P (proper prefix of T): lowercase(P) != lowercase(T) since lengths differ, so an entry tagged T (and not tagged P) fails the whole-tag test → excluded from run 4. Rule: '--list prints every aphorism in the filtered set in corpus order' → order = harvest order. Rule: 'Empty candidate set after filtering is an error... exit code 1, a human-readable message on stderr, and zero bytes on stdout' → applies when S_P is empty. Rule: 'When combined with --list, --json emits one JSON object per line... for each entry in the filtered set, in corpus order' → NDJSON comparison is valid.

scenarios.title: --author substring filter and --author+--tag AND-intersection, verified as exact set algebra over the listing
scenarios.why_this_surface: Attacks the two-filter interaction (AND, not OR) and the substring-vs-exact author contrast, where implementations plausibly OR the filters or require exact author equality.
steps: Harvest: run --list --json; parse all entries.

Pick an author name from the harvest; let A be an interior fragment of it (not the full name, e.g. characters 2..5) with its letter case flipped. Pick a tag T carried by at least one entry. Compute from the harvest: S_A = entries whose author contains A case-insensitively; S_T = entries with whole tag T (case-insensitive); S_AT = S_A intersect S_T, all in harvest order.
Run --list --json --author A; compare to S_A exactly.
Run --list --json --tag T; compare to S_T exactly.
Run --list --json --author A --tag T; compare to S_AT exactly — and specifically confirm it is NOT the union when S_A union S_T is strictly larger than S_AT.

commands.note: harvest for computing expected sets
A = case-flipped interior fragment of a harvested author name
T = harvested tag
both filters — must be the intersection of the two previous runs

assumptions: Executor picks A and T from the harvest, so S_A and S_T are non-empty by construction (detectable: the harvest is in hand).

If possible, pick A and T such that S_A != S_T (so union differs from intersection and the AND/OR distinction is observable); if no such pair exists in the corpus, report the scenario as inconclusive rather than passed.
scenarios.expected: Run 2: exit 0; emitted sequence equals S_A exactly (every emitted author contains A case-insensitively; no harvest entry satisfying that test is missing; order = harvest order). Run 3: exit 0; equals S_T exactly. Run 4: exit 0 if S_AT non-empty (guaranteed non-empty if T was chosen from an entry inside S_A; otherwise exit 1 with empty stdout and stderr message, per the computed S_AT); emitted sequence equals S_AT exactly — every entry appears in BOTH run 2's and run 3's output, and every entry common to runs 2 and 3 appears, in harvest order. Nothing on stderr for any exit-0 run.
scenarios.discriminator: An OR implementation emits S_A ∪ S_T in run 4 (strictly larger than the intersection under the chosen A,T); an exact-match author comparator emits nothing for the fragment A (wrong exit 1); a case-sensitive author matcher also empties S_A since A's case is flipped.
scenarios.derivation: Rule: '--author matches by substring containment, case-insensitively, against the aphorism's author field (e.g., --author dijk matches "Edsger W. Dijkstra").' A is a substring of a harvested author with case flipped → that entry is in S_A; the membership test for every entry is lowercase(author).includes(lowercase(A)). Rule: '--tag matches a whole tag, case-insensitively' → S_T as computed. Rule: 'Supplying both narrows to the intersection (AND, not OR).' → run 4 = S_A ∩ S_T, no more, no less. Rule: '--list prints every aphorism in the filtered set in corpus order' + '--json ... one JSON object per line ... in corpus order' → exact ordered-sequence comparison is licensed. Rule: empty intersection ⇒ 'exit code 1, a human-readable message on stderr, and zero bytes on stdout.'

scenarios.title: No-match is exit 1 with silent stdout — including under --json, which must not emit empty JSON
scenarios.why_this_surface: Attacks the no-match x --json interaction: a plausible implementation prints '{}', 'null', or '[]' to stdout with exit 0, or reuses the usage exit code 2, instead of the mandated 1/stderr/empty-stdout triple.
steps: Confirm from the harvest of --list --json (scenario 3/4, or run it here) that no author contains the probe string and no entry carries the probe tag — this makes the assumption checkable instead of silently vacuous.
Run the author probe without --json; record exit code and both streams byte-exactly.
Run the tag probe with --json; record exit code and both streams byte-exactly.
Run the combined author+tag probe with a REAL harvested author fragment plus the impossible tag: intersection with an empty set is empty, so same error triple.

commands.note: assumption check: verify probe strings match nothing in the corpus
empty candidate set, plain mode
empty candidate set with --json — stdout must still be zero bytes, not '{}' or '[]'
nonempty author set AND empty tag set → empty intersection → same error

assumptions: 'qxzv-no-such-author-31337' is a substring of no author and 'qxzv-no-such-tag-31337' is a whole tag of no entry — verified against the run-1 harvest, so a violated assumption is detected, not silently passed.
<real-author-fragment> is taken from the harvest and matches at least one entry.
scenarios.expected: Runs 2, 3 and 4 each: exit code exactly 1 (not 0, not 2), stdout is exactly zero bytes (not '{}', not '[]', not 'null', not an empty line), stderr contains a non-empty human-readable message. Run 1: exit 0 and used only for assumption verification.
scenarios.discriminator: A faked implementation that treats no-match as success (exit 0 with empty or placeholder JSON), or that lumps it with usage errors as exit 2, or that prints the error to stdout, fails on at least one of the three exact observables (exit==1, stdout byte-count==0, stderr non-empty) in each run.
scenarios.derivation: Rule: 'Empty candidate set after filtering is an error, not an empty success: exit code 1, a human-readable message on stderr, and zero bytes on stdout.' Run 2: no author contains the probe (verified) → candidate set empty → the triple applies. Run 3: no entry has the probe as a whole tag → empty set; '--json ... composes with the filter and seed flags' gives --json no license to change the error contract, and 'Errors go to stderr, never stdout' forbids any stdout bytes → same triple. Run 4: 'Supplying both narrows to the intersection (AND, not OR)'; S_author ∩ ∅ = ∅ → empty set → same triple. Exit-code table separates this from usage: '0 success, 1 no match, 2 bad usage' → exactly 1, not 2.

scenarios.title: Usage errors (unknown flag, missing seed argument) exit 2 cleanly, while --json --seed emits exactly one parseable NDJSON-compatible line
scenarios.why_this_surface: Attacks the exit-code taxonomy (2 vs 1 vs 0) for the two non-seed usage triggers and the single-selection --json shape, where implementations often print help to stdout, exit 1 for everything, or pretty-print multi-line JSON.
steps: Run with an unknown flag; record exit code and both streams.
Run with --seed as the final token and no value; record exit code and both streams.
Run --json with a valid seed; verify stdout is a single line that parses as one JSON object with the required keys, and that the run is deterministic (repeat once).
Verify stderr is empty and exit is 0 on the successful runs.

commands.note: unknown flag → bad usage
missing flag argument → bad usage
valid composition: one single-line JSON object
repeat — must be byte-identical (determinism)

assumptions: '--frobnicate' is not a supported flag (the spec enumerates exactly six flags: --author, --tag, --seed, --list, --json, --help).
scenarios.expected: Run 1: exit code exactly 2, zero bytes on stdout (help/usage text, if any, must not go to stdout on the error path per 'Errors go to stderr, never stdout'), non-empty stderr. Run 2: exit code exactly 2, zero bytes on stdout, non-empty stderr. Runs 3 and 4: exit 0, empty stderr, stdout is exactly one line (exactly one newline-terminated record, no pretty-printed multi-line JSON, no banner) which JSON.parse accepts as an object having at minimum string-valued 'text', string-valued 'author', and array-valued 'tags'; runs 3 and 4 byte-identical.
scenarios.discriminator: An implementation that exits 1 for all errors, prints usage help to stdout, or pretty-prints JSON across multiple lines fails the exact exit-2/empty-stdout/single-line observables; a hardcoded fake without real structured corpus data cannot emit a well-formed object with all three keys that also stays stable under the seed.
scenarios.derivation: Exit-code rule: '2 bad usage (unknown flag, missing flag argument, or seed value that Number() parses to NaN).' --frobnicate is outside the enumerated flag set → 'unknown flag' → exit 2; bare --seed has no value token → 'missing flag argument' → exit 2. Taste rule: 'Errors go to stderr, never stdout' → both usage errors put their message on stderr and leave stdout at zero bytes. Rule: '--json emits the selected aphorism as a single-line JSON object with at minimum the keys text, author, and tags; it composes with the filter and seed flags' → run 3 stdout = one line, parseable, three keys; corpus rule 'structured data (text, author, tags)' fixes their types. Determinism rule: 'the same seed and the same filtered candidate set always yield the same aphorism' → run 3 == run 4 byte-for-byte.
